IM5 = item 5 follows the questionnaire's presentation order. That assignment is confirmed against the data: the same paper's Table 8 publishes a mean and an SD for each item, and the live data reproduces all ten values (IM1 4.111/0.885, IM2 4.200/0.815, IM3 4.356/0.830, IM4 4.200/0.842, IM5 4.244/0.830 against published 4.11/0.885, 4.20/0.815, 4.36/0.830, 4.20/0.842, 4.24/0.830), and because the five published mean-SD pairs are all different from one another, no other assignment of the five sentences to the five codes fits. The response coding is not inferred either -- the deposit ships each item as both a label and an integer and the two agree cell for cell (2 = disagree, 3 = ordinary, 4 = agree, 5 = strongly agree; 1 = strongly disagree was never used by any respondent). Two caveats on the wording itself: the questionnaire was administered in Chinese and only the authors' English is published, so English is what ships here; and the paper prints item 2 two ways, as "I would use the app to learn more about sports if time permits" in Table 1 and as "If time permits, I would use the app to learn more about sports" in Table 8. The Table 1 form is what ships, since it is the measurement-item table and the S1 Table supplement reproduces it in that form.
